docs.title: MSF React
docs.text: This repository is the React workspace for the MSF ecosystem. It organizes app and package code in a pnpm workspace so shared frontend libraries and app experiences can evolve independently while staying aligned with a consistent design system and tooling stack.

docs.title: Repository purpose
docs.text:
The workspace is structured to support:

  • reusable React packages under packages/
  • app-level demos and previews under apps/
  • shared tooling and build configuration under configs/
  • a coordinated frontend development workflow using pnpm workspaces

docs.title: Repository shape
docs.text:
react/
├── apps/
├── configs/
├── packages/
├── scripts/
├── package.json
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── pnpm-lock.yaml
├── README.md
├── mkdocs.yml
├── .github/
└── openwiki/

docs.title: Typical workspace commands
docs.text:
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm lint
pnpm test

docs.title: Operational guidance
docs.text:
• keep shared UI logic inside the package layer when possible
  • use app directories for concrete experiences or demos
  • document package boundaries clearly for contributors
  • prefer workspace scripts and shared configs over repo-specific duplication

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text: The react repository is designed as a modular frontend workspace. It demonstrates the MSF pattern of separating reusable UI packages from app-level experiences while keeping a common build and release flow.

docs.title: Primary responsibilities
docs.text:
This workspace is meant to provide:

  • shared React modules and components
  • workspace-level tooling for build and linting
  • a playground or app layer for local validation
  • reusable packaging conventions for frontend packages

docs.title: Key configuration
docs.text:
The repo uses pnpm workspaces and a shared package manager setup:

"packageManager": "pnpm@10.29.2",
"workspaces": [
  "packages/*"
]

docs.title: Development workflow
docs.text:
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm --dir apps/playground dev

docs.title: Guidance for contributors
docs.text:
• keep package APIs small and well-scoped
  • use shared configs where possible
  • document app-specific constraints separately from reusable package code
  • validate changes using the workspace scripts before release
